header: Date: 2027-10-05 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Sofia Alvarez (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Karen Blake (Everest Procurement), Ravi Patel (Everest Legal), Monica Li (Everest Security), Tom Reyes (Everest ML)
summary: Procurement-focused call to review MSA and DPA redlines, confirm SLA targets, discuss pricing approval path and vendor onboarding steps. Redwood AE + SE clarified documents to send, Everest legal/procurement to return redlines and approval timeline. Action items agreed for SOC2/SLA sharing and bench testing details.
topics: DPA: data residency, encryption, deletion and subprocessors
SLA uptime, latency SLOs, credits and uptime measurement
Pricing approvals: PO path and finance signoff
Onboarding: SCIM/SSO, SOC2 artifacts, benchmark access
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Alvarez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time. I'm Sofia, I'm the AE on the account, and with me is Marcus our systems engineer.
[00:08] Marcus Chen: Hi all. Quick heads up I'm going to stay fairly technical on the SLA and the benchmark bits.
[00:15] Karen Blake: Thanks, Sofia. We have Ravi and Monica here from legal and security, and Tom from the ML team. We're hoping to get a clear path to sign - procurement timeline is the main driver.
[00:25] Sofia Alvarez: Great. Agenda - MSA redlines, DPA questions, SLA specifics, pricing and procurement path, and then actions. Sound good?
[00:33] Tom Reyes: Yep. For the ML team we want to make sure the SLOs are realistic for 99th percentile latency, and also that we can run benchmarks before commit.
[00:41] Ravi Patel: From legal we'll focus on indemnity, liability caps, data processing details in the DPA, and subprocessors.
[00:48] Sofia Alvarez: Perfect. Let's start with the MSA. We received your marked-up MSA draft yesterday, correct?
[00:55] Karen Blake: Yes, sent through last night, marked a few clauses we want to adjust. I think Ravi will walk through.
[01:02] Ravi Patel: Right. Main ask is to tighten liability for data breaches to 2x fees or a fixed cap - we cited industry comps. Also we want clearer audit rights and data return/deletion zones. One addition: require notification of subprocessors 30 days before onboarding.
[01:18] Marcus Chen: Quick clarifying question on subprocessors - are you talking about infra partners like cloud regions or model providers?
[01:24] Ravi Patel: Both. We want visibility if you use a third-party model provider or a new cloud region that may change data residency.
[01:31] Sofia Alvarez: Understood. We typically disclose primary cloud providers in the DPA and will notify for major changes. For subprocessors there is a carve for operational partners; we can add a 30-day notice clause for new ones that affect data residency.
[01:44] Monica Li: On data residency, we need to make sure production PII stays in us-east or eu-west depending on the dataset. Can Redwood guarantee region pinning for Dedicated or Private deployments?
[01:55] Marcus Chen: Yes - on Dedicated you can pin workloads to a region and we support Private (VPC/on-prem) for full residency. Hosted will have region options but there are some constraints for model availability.
[02:07] Tom Reyes: For benchmarking we need a hosted-like environment to run our request patterns. Is there a standard benchmark plan Redwood runs?
[02:14] Marcus Chen: We have a performance kit; I can share a benchmark plan and a test cluster access flow. We usually do a 48-hour test with representative queries, record p99 latency, throughput, and cost per token.
[02:25] Ravi Patel: Back to MSA - indemnity language: Redwood's current draft limits indemnity to claims arising from Redwood's gross negligence. We want standard warranty and indemnity for data breaches caused by vendor negligence.
[02:36] Sofia Alvarez: We can accept indemnity for vendor negligence. For caps, we need to check finance policy - typical Redwood policy caps to 2x annual fees for SaaS customers, but we can discuss a mutual cap or carveouts for data breach and IP.
[02:49] Karen Blake: Finance will push for a fixed cap figure, we need numbers to run through procurement.
[02:55] Sofia Alvarez: Understood - we'll propose a couple of options in writing. I'll include a 2x-fees option and a fixed-dollar option so you can model either.
[03:03] Karen Blake: That helps. On the DPA side, Ravi noted data deletion - what is Redwood's retention policy and ability to purge logs on request?
[03:12] Marcus Chen: For hosted logs we retain request logs for 90 days by default, can be configured via entitlements. On Dedicated/Private you control retention; for deletion we support on-demand deletion requests and can provide proof of deletion for customer-controlled deployments.
[03:25] Monica Li: We need retention under 90 days for some PII datasets, ideally 30 days. Is that configurable on hosted?
[03:32] Sofia Alvarez: For hosted customers at enterprise tier we can offer custom retention SLAs; for Dedicated/Private it's configurable. I'll note that as a requirement in the follow-up.
[03:42] Tom Reyes: SLA specifics - we care about two things: uptime and 99th percentile latency for inference. Can we get an explicit p99 latency SLO with credit calculations?
[03:51] Marcus Chen: We can define p99 latency targets per model class and sequence length buckets. Credits are typically pro-rated monthly if we miss uptime SLA. For latency SLOs, we generally offer guidance and operational commitments rather than financial credits, but for Dedicated we can commit to latency targets with defined remediation.
[04:05] Ravi Patel: Our engineering leadership wants contractual latency credits for production critical routes. Is Redwood open to latency credits for Dedicated?
[04:12] Marcus Chen: We can include latency credits for Dedicated with measurable metrics, e.g., p99 below X ms for 8k tokens; if missed three times in a quarter trigger remediation credits. We'll need to work out specific thresholds.
[04:24] Sofia Alvarez: I'll include a detailed SLA matrix showing uptime %, incident MTTR targets, and proposed latency bands for dedicated tiers.
[04:32] Karen Blake: Pricing approvals - finance will need a PO. We have a couple of internal gates: procurement approves vendor, finance approves spend, legal signs MSA. What's Redwood's standard procurement paperwork?
[04:43] Sofia Alvarez: We provide standard SOW/pricing sheet and an invoice template. We can accept PO and have enterprise billing options. If you want metered billing vs committed reserved capacity, we can show both pricing layouts.
[04:54] Karen Blake: We'll likely go committed for Dedicated for predictable cost. Need committed pricing and overage terms.
[05:01] Sofia Alvarez: We'll send committed pricing tiers and overage rules. Also, if you want a reserved instance style commit, there's a discount ladder based on commit size.
[05:09] Tom Reyes: One quick item - can you support SSO/SCIM so we can onboard teams quickly?
[05:14] Marcus Chen: Yes, SSO via SAML/OIDC and SCIM for provisioning. We also support role-based access controls. I'll include a SCIM onboarding checklist.
[05:23] Ravi Patel: Do you retain IP for any prompts or derived models? We need explicit no-rights-taking language in MSA.
[05:29] Sofia Alvarez: Redwood's position is customer retains their input and outputs; we don't assert model ownership. We'll add a clause to the MSA clarifying customer data ownership and usage.
[05:38] Monica Li: Encryption at rest and in transit - are keys customer-managed?
[05:42] Marcus Chen: We support KMS integrations (customer-managed keys) in Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted can use customer KMS for encryption keys in enterprise plans.
[05:51] Karen Blake: Ok. Timeline - procurement needs final MSA and DPA signed to issue PO; our internal cadence wants a signature by 2027-10-15 to hit next quarter budget. Is that feasible?
[06:02] Sofia Alvarez: Yes, assuming we get redlines back early next week. Suggested timeline: you send redlines by 2027-10-12, we respond within 2 business days, finalize DPA and SLA then send for signature.
[06:13] Ravi Patel: We can try to return redlines by 10/12 but may come earlier.
[06:17] Sofia Alvarez: Great. Marcus, do you want to walk through the benchmark approach?
[06:21] Marcus Chen: Sure. We'll provide a test cluster with subset of model variants; you'll run your traffic patterns for 48 hours. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 and token cost. We also measure cold-starts and KV/prefix cache behavior. For fairness we ask for representative prompts and sequence length distribution.
[06:36] Tom Reyes: We'll provide a dataset and traffic profile. One question - if we find quality regressions between model versions, is there an easy rollback or pin?
[06:45] Marcus Chen: Yes, the runtime supports pinning to model versions and automatic fallbacks to compatible variants. We'll include a rollout policy example in the docs.
[06:53] Karen Blake: On security docs - please send SOC2 report, ISO certification summary, and any penetration test summaries.
[06:58] Sofia Alvarez: Will do. I'll attach them to an email and include the SLA matrix.
[07:03] Ravi Patel: A quick note on subprocessors again - 30-day notice is fine but we need the ability to object if a subprocessor materially changes risk. Can we add an objection window?
[07:14] Sofia Alvarez: We can add a notice plus a defined objection window, say 10 business days, with escalation to our security team. If there's a material risk we can offer mitigation or an alternate arrangement (e.g., region pinning or Private deployment).
[07:26] Monica Li: That sounds workable. Also audit rights - we may require an on-site or remote audit annually for Dedicated. Is that supported?
[07:33] Marcus Chen: For Dedicated and Private, remote audits and evidence are supported; on-site audits can be arranged but we usually prefer remote with evidence packages. We'll include acceptable audit artifacts.
[07:44] Karen Blake: Any outstanding legal terms we haven't covered?
[07:48] Ravi Patel: A couple: termination for convenience notice period - we prefer 60 days, your default is 30. Also transition assistance post-termination - require 90 days of assistance.
[07:58] Sofia Alvarez: We can be flexible - 60 days is reasonable for enterprise. Transition assistance of 90 days we can include as a priced add-on or include in the first year for enterprise customers. I'll propose language.
[08:12] Tom Reyes: Great. From a technical point, once MSA is signed we want access to the test cluster within 5 business days. Is that doable?
[08:20] Marcus Chen: Yes, provided we have cleared credit and provisioning details; Dedicated provisioning can take longer though. For hosted test clusters we can usually provision within 72 hours.
[08:29] Karen Blake: Final bit - pricing approvals: do you require a signed MSA before issuing invoice and accepting PO?
[08:36] Sofia Alvarez: We require a signed MSA and DPA for account creation and billing for enterprise; for pilots we can do a short-term agreement. For committed capacity purchase we'll need the PO and signed MSA.
[08:46] Karen Blake: Okay. Sounds like next steps are clear.
[08:50] Sofia Alvarez: Recap - I'll send SOC2/ISO and SLA matrix tomorrow (2027-10-06). Ravi to return redlines by 10/12. Marcus will send benchmark plan and SCIM checklist by 10/08. Karen will start procurement and aim for decision by 10/15.
[09:04] Ravi Patel: Sounds good.
[09:06] Monica Li: Thanks everyone.
[09:08] Tom Reyes: Thanks, talk soon.
[09:10] Sofia Alvarez: Thanks - we'll follow up via email with artifacts.

Note: transcription includes occasional mis-hearings and name variants; timestamps approximate.
